items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy Lunceford's band and my band, we were something like brothers... We were very close.

ctx.x: and all of that that you have on trumpet. I mean, that's not very easy. I mean, it isn't even possible for everybody to do that. Now, how did you go about that?

Well, I heard Steve, [Tommy Stevenson] Ben Stevens. I think he was playing trumpet with Jimmy Lunceford. And, I tried it with the mouthpiece that I had. You know, a regular mouthpiece, and I couldn't make it.

So, right then, it seemed like it was too small. I couldn't find one that was cut large enough for me. So, I took an old mouthpiece, took a file, sandpaper, put it on the paper, shaved it down, took the file and filed it down, cut it out, made that, made it a little wider, a little shallower inside. And, I kept on doing it until I got it the way my mouth felt comfortable. And then, I took it to a place and let them smooth it down, then played it.

Oh, yes. We did, especially when we were together at the Savoy cause when Chick would go on, he'd go and play 45 minutes. And then, when he'd take his break, I was on for 45 minutes. So, that's the same audience. They were standing right in front of the band all the same time. And the people, they liked, they liked us both. And, they showed it. They enjoyed it. Cause, take for instance, Ella Fitzgerald, at the time she was nothing but a kid at the time. Sixteen or 17 years old, I believe. And, we got her out of…

contest there, I believe.
So, we all shared the same audience
together. Sometimes, we were by ourselves. But,
the same people would come there. I'm just
speaking of the Savoy alone. And then if we go
to the theaters, we used to get the same respect
from the people that you'd get from other bands.
I did the same thing with Jimmie
Lunceford. We, I had a tune out called "Do You
Wanna Jump Children". That was in 1939, too, I
believe. Jimmie Lunceford had a tune out, that
was a big seller for me at that time.…
mine. Then, we alternated during the rest of the night. Then, we did tunes together. And then I had to put on my big show.
